Torres wore again the helmet he had filched from his withered ancestor in the Chamber of the Mummies. Their greeting was instant and warm, taking the form of a flight of arrows that arched into them and stretched two of the followers on the ground. Next, the Lost Souls, men and women, charged; while the rifles of Torres’ men began to speak. So unexpected was this charge, so swiftly made and with so short a distance to cover, that, though many fell before the bullets, a number reached the invaders and engaged in a desperate hand-to-hand conflict. All looked and saw, not fifty yards away, Torres, the Jefe, and their gang of followers, emerging into the open clearing. Torres wore again the helmet he had filched from his withered ancestor in the Chamber of the Mummies. Their greeting was instant and warm, taking the form of a flight of arrows that arched into them and stretched two of the followers on the ground. Next, the Lost Souls, men and women, charged; while the rifles of Torres’ men began to speak. So unexpected was this charge, so swiftly made and with so short a distance to cover, that, though many fell before the bullets, a number reached the invaders and engaged in a desperate hand-to-hand conflict. The survivors fled, but of the invaders half were down and down forever. The women having in drastic fashion attended to every man who fell wounded. The Jefe was spluttering with pain and rage at an arrow which had perforated his arm; nor could he be appeased until Vicente cut off the barbed head and pulled out the shaft.", "sha256": "01d83be164231aa43cd232f9889c1c8e3613dcdf7959cbb95c83d01f9b19f6b6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[2460]", "source_html": "

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u029-r0019", "tag": "p", "text": "Since there were no wounded of their own to be attended to with rough and ready surgery, Torres and the Jefe led the way to the lake, skirted its shores, and came to the ruins of the Queen’s dwelling. Only charred stumps of piles, projecting above the water, showed where it had once stood. Torres was nonplussed, but the Jefe was furious.", "sha256": "af9f876c333b37b8bc26ac1f95f46be4b92387b695d61a2bb477a06355021f17", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[2462]", "source_html": "

Since there were no wounded of their own to be attended to with rough and ready surgery, Torres and the Jefe led the way to the lake, skirted its shores, and came to the ruins of the Queen’s dwelling. Only charred stumps of piles, projecting above the water, showed where it had once stood. Torres was nonplussed, but the Jefe was furious.

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u029-r0020", "tag": "p", "text": "“Here, right in this house that was, the treasure chest stood,” he stammered.", "sha256": "8300347ec038fd6cc72f38c4e5741ff79460259b36cbe6956922d1efcea29fef", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[2463]", "source_html": "

“Here, right in this house that was, the treasure chest stood,” he stammered.

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u029-r0021", "tag": "p", "text": "“A wild goose chase!” the Jefe grunted. “Senor Torres, I always suspected you were a fool.”", "sha256": "0cf52e1702d6e6cfc8065568704a081332d9498271ee2b23361b131b9fe60fa3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[2464]", "source_html": "

“A wild goose chase!” the Jefe grunted. “Senor Torres, I always suspected you were a fool.”

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u029-r0022", "tag": "p", "text": "“How was I to know the place had been burned down?”", "sha256": "71cc84410948c55493a5856f15b74f9eda1b92785e35cb6fa356bacf077cb1e1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[2465]", "source_html": "

“How was I to know the place had been burned down?”

I had my eye on you. I saw you rob the emeralds and rubies from the eye-sockets of the Maya gods. That much you shall divide with me, and now.”", "sha256": "892bffb41ce99effb7e7c5e089c1c24500053d7934f3912d364837bd21418365", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[2466]", "source_html": "

“You ought to have known, you who are so very wise in all things,” the Jefe bickered back. “But you can’t fool me. I had my eye on you. I saw you rob the emeralds and rubies from the eye-sockets of the Maya gods. That much you shall divide with me, and now.”

The chest may have fallen into the water undamaged by fire when the roof fell in.
